summary: A Reuters report republished by Allwork.Space covers a 24-hour general strike in Italy called by the grassroots union Unione Sindacale di Base, with protests planned in more than 40 cities. Tens of thousands of people, mostly students and workers, marched to demand higher wages and stronger public services, to protest the rising cost of living, and to oppose increased military spending. The demonstrations followed earlier clashes in which protesters fought police, looted shops and vandalised property, but were largely peaceful this time, with tensions flaring in some locations. In Turin, police deployed a water cannon against students and left-wing activists who approached security cordons around the prefecture building. In Rome, a large march passed near the Colosseum, where protesters said they intended to pitch tents and stay through the weekend; rubbish bins were placed across streets and set alight. In the evening a large group attempted to march on parliament, prompting police to use water cannon to disperse them, according to Italian news agency ANSA, which also reported eight detentions after repeated attempts to breach police barricades. In Milan, protesters marched onto the ring road and ended in front of the Politecnico di Milano university, carrying flares and setting fire to objects. In Genoa, around 15,000 port workers, students and other demonstrators entered the port, echoing similar protests in Europe and elsewhere against the use of ports for arms shipments and drawing attention to seafarer deaths in conflicts from the Gulf to the Black Sea. The piece notes a broader wave of protests across European countries including France, Spain, Belgium and Albania, driven by grievances including the cost of living. The item is pure labour and political news with no workplace technology, facilities, or hybrid work content.

claims.claim: A 24-hour general strike was called in Italy with protests planned in more than 40 cities
claims.attribution: Unione Sindacale di Base (grassroots union), via Reuters
